Public liability vs professional indemnity: what is the difference?

Chestnut Insurance Agency editorial team · Published 21 November 2026

Public liability deals with physical harm: injury to a person or damage to property. Professional indemnity deals with financial loss caused by mistakes in advice or professional services. Many businesses need one, and professional firms often need both.

The difference in one example

A visitor trips over a cable in your consulting office and breaks a wrist. That is a public liability matter. A client loses money because your report contained an error. That is a professional indemnity matter.

Side by side

  • Public liability: bodily injury or property damage to third parties, linked to your premises or activities
  • Professional indemnity: financial loss to clients from negligent advice, design or services
  • Public liability is usually occurrence-based, PI is often claims-made
  • Contracts may require either or both, with minimum limits

Which do you need?

If you are unsure, bring your contracts and a description of your services. A short review will show the gaps.

  • A shop or restaurant: public liability matters most
  • A contractor: public liability plus contractors all risks, and PI if you provide design
  • A consultant, accountant or advocate: PI first, and public liability if clients visit you
  • A clinic: PI and public liability

This guide is general education about insurance in Kenya. It is not legal or financial advice and does not describe any specific policy. Policy wording, exclusions and the law that applies at the time govern. Speak to an advisor about your situation.
